transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya, Liam, Marisol

Summary (auto-gen, brief): quick security posture discovery for potential Private/Dedicated deployment; cover SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS and retention, then next steps.

00:00:03 Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood Inference, im the account exec, with miguel our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:00:10 Priya: good thanks, Priya here. busy day, appreciate you fitting us in.
00:00:15 Marisol: hi, marisol — cto — i'll be short, want to make sure this maps to our security controls.
00:00:22 Miguel: great, thanks. quick agenda: baseline questions about your stack and controls, then dive into specific ask: SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS and retention, then next steps. sound good?
00:00:32 Liam: yep that's perfect.

02:12 Priya: quick context — we are building an internal recommendations service using LLMs, currently run on GCP and AWS for different teams. latency is important but security is a blocker for hosted api. we want to understand if hosted is acceptable, or if dedicated/private is required.
02:40 Avery: makes sense. what compliance requirements do you have today? do you maintain SOC2? HIPAA?
02:48 Priya: we have SOC2 Type II in scope and PCI for payments team, but the recommendations service will touch PII-ish metadata so SOC2 is the primary. we also have SSO via okta.
03:05 Miguel: ok good, three main areas typically: 1) do you need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), 2) network isolation (VPC or on-prem), and 3) auditability / log retention. for each we have hosted, dedicated, and private options.

05:20 Liam: for us key ownership is important — we need to ensure encryption at rest with a customer-managed key and key rotation policies, ideally HSM-backed. does Redwood support CMK right now?
05:34 Miguel: yes, for Private we support customer-managed keys with HSM via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault integrations. for Dedicated we offer a bring-your-own-kms option for select contracts, and Hosted has envelope encryption with keys managed by Redwood but we can discuss advanced options. note: some language in our docs varies — we call the feature Redbud — uh redwood key manager in older docs so apologies for any naming confusions.
06:05 Priya: hmm ok for initial pilot we'd consider Dedicated if the KMS guarantees are there.

08:15 Marisol: about SSO — we use Okta and need SAML 2.0 for console access and also SCIM provisioning for user sync. do you support SCIM?
08:25 Avery: yes we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning in our enterprise offering. for Hosted customers we have SSO w SAML and SCIM via the console; Dedicated/Private provide same but with customer-managed IdP integrations and longer session controls.

10:00 Liam: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles, separation between model operators, dev, and auditors. how granular is RBAC? can we integrate with Okta group claims?
10:12 Miguel: RBAC is role + group based; we map Okta groups to Redwood roles and support custom roles for restricted actions, and audit logs show token-level activity. caveat: some older audit logs may have truncated user agents in legacy pipelines.
10:30 Priya: that's fine as long as the main actions are logged — create model, deploy, key ops, API key access, runtime requests?
10:40 Miguel: runtime requests are logged at a token/route level for Dedicated/Private, Hosted has aggregated token-level cost and trace logs; we also provide optional request-level audit logs for enterprise with retention options.

14:50 Liam: retention — we have regulatory constraints: default 90 days for logs, some datasets need 7 year retention. can you segregate retention by dataset or route?
15:05 Avery: yes, retention can be configured per-route for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has tiered retention options and we can push logs to your log archive (S3/GCS) for long-term storage. export pipelines can be set up.

18:40 Marisol: what about data residency — our legal requires data processed in EU. can you pin region?
18:50 Miguel: yes, we have region pinning for Hosted models in EU regions, Dedicated provides physical pools in region, and Private is fully customer-controlled. some open model variants may only be available in certain regions due to licensing, but we can work with you on model choices.

22:30 Priya: auditability — do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed audit trails?
22:40 Miguel: we provide signed logs where required — we integrate with customer KMS for signing in Private, and for Dedicated we can configure advanced auditing. Hosted has standard audit trails and integrations with SIEM via syslog/forwarders.

26:00 Liam: encryption in transit — mTLS? do you support mutual TLS for API calls from our services?
26:10 Avery: mTLS is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted uses TLS 1.3 and we can enable client certs for customer endpoints in Dedicated.

29:50 Priya: incident response — how quickly do you notify customers for security incidents, and do you provide runbooks?
30:00 Avery: SLA for security incident notification is 72 hours to initial ack, with escalation paths for P1. we provide SOC2 report and an incident response summary for enterprise contracts. we'll include our IR runbook link in the follow-up.

33:15 Liam: penetration testing — can we run pentests against Dedicated or Private? any restrictions?
33:25 Miguel: yes, for Dedicated/Private customers we allow pentesting with a standard sign-off; Hosted has limited scope and we handle pentests at platform level and share results. must coordinate with SRE to avoid disruptions.

36:05 Marisol: licensing and vendor lock — if we start on Dedicated and later want to move on-prem, how hard is migration?
36:15 Miguel: migration is supported; Private deployment uses same control plane APIs and configs, but data-plane transfer requires roadmap planning. we have migration playbooks and model artifact export tooling.

39:40 Liam: ok can we talk about network diagrams — we need a VPC peering option and private link.
39:50 Avery: yes we support VPC peering, Private Link and customer controlled ingress. we'll share a sample network diagram (link: https://redwood.ai/security/networksample). note: link is internal doc ref.

42:10 Priya: curious about token-level logs — you said hosted aggregates, can you give an example?
42:18 Miguel: sure, hosted returns aggregated usage and per-request trace ids but not full payload storage by default; we have an opt-in request-logging add-on that stores request/response with pii redaction. Dedicated/Private can be configured to persist full traces in your own archive.

45:55 Marisol: ok, last question around SOC2 and ISO — do you have copies of Type II and ISO 27001 attestation we can share with procurement?
46:05 Avery: yes, we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation for the platform. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and full attestations in follow up and share our security portal link.

48:30 Priya: will you be able to send us a run of required docs for legal — vulnerability management, third-party risk, subprocessor list?
48:40 Avery: absolutely, we have a security package for enterprise prospects that includes vulnerability program, subprocessor list, privacy policy, DPA template, and encryption notes.

50:00 Recap (Avery): action items — we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, network diagram, KMS options, RBAC notes, sample audit logs, and pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Priya will confirm pilot stakeholders and timeline.
50:20 Priya: sounds good, i'll schedule a follow-up with infra and security next week.
50:30 Marisol: thanks everyone.
50:35 Liam: thanks.
50:40 Avery: thanks team, we'll follow up with materials in a few days.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hears (Redbud vs Redwood, product name variants), typical of auto-transcript. Shared artifacts: SOC2 report (link provided in follow-up), network diagram (redwood.ai/security/networksample), RBAC notes (attached in email).
